It reduces ray-segment list length and manipulation cost by ordering cells according to their center of gravity depth [S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the method reduces ray-segment list length and manipulation cost by ordering cells according to their center of gravity depth. Source [S2] explicitly states: 'Our solution to this issue is approximate depth sorting which sorts the cells in the depth order of their center of gravity.' It further explains that processing cells in depth-sorted order 'could reduce the length of the ray-segment list, and thus it could reduce the list manipulation cost at the same time.' The source also notes that this approach avoids the computational cost associated with more complex sorting methods (like octree search) to achieve near-perfect order. Therefore, every fact in the claim is supported by the evidence.

Both sources confirm the specific techniques and justifications mentioned in the claim.
